youtube.baslik: When sound reaches you, do the air molecules travel to your ear? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: As sound travels, air molecules do not travel from the source to the ear; each molecule moves back and forth around its own rest position and passes the motion to its neighbor. What travels is the pattern of compression and rarefaction, that is, energy; so sound is not a flow of air like wind.

cumleler: When sound reaches you, do the air molecules travel to your ear?
No; each molecule only oscillates back and forth around its rest position.
The oscillating molecule passes its motion to its neighbor.
What travels is the pattern of compression and rarefaction, that is, energy.
Like a stadium wave: fans stay put, while the wave moves on.
So sound is not a flow of air like wind.
